# dtcloud_lb_vms (Data Source)

Lists the machines on a network that can be added to a pool as members.

This is the lookup the web console offers when you pick members, and it is what makes a `for_each`
member set possible without pasting ids.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The machines on a network that can be added to a pool. This is the lookup the
# web console offers when you pick members, and it is what makes a `for_each`
# member set possible.
data "dtcloud_lb_vms" "candidates" {
  network_id = dtcloud_network.app.id
}

output "candidates" {
  # A machine can hold several addresses on one network, so `ip_addresses` is a list.
  value = [for vm in data.dtcloud_lb_vms.candidates.vms : "${vm.name}  ${join(",", vm.ip_addresses)}"]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `network_id` (String) Network to look for candidate members on.

### Optional

- `pool_id` (String) When set, VMs already in this pool are left out of the result.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `vms` (List of Object) VMs attached to the network. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--vms))

<a id="nestedatt--vms"></a>
### Nested Schema for `vms`

Read-Only:

- `id` (String)
- `ip_address` (String)
- `ip_addresses` (List of String)
- `name` (String)

## Behaviour worth knowing

* **`ip_addresses` is a list, not a single field.** The platform builds it from every port the machine
  holds on that network, and a machine with three addresses on one network is ordinary. `ip_address`
  is the first of them; name the one you want in `dtcloud_lb_member.address`.
* **`pool_id` filters out machines already in that pool**, which is what keeps a `for_each` set from
  proposing members that exist.
